answer: A credential starts with a 50-credit burn and a 120-credit bond locked for 36 epochs. The relic contract issues only 96 seats and binds each key to one receipt. A shale beacon schedules three service jobs on separate days; a copper accumulator publishes task hashes and nullifiers. Five of seven established reviewers must reproduce the signed traces before activation. Each extra identity therefore pays another burn, locks another bond, completes fresh work, and gains a new quorum; reused or missed proofs burn 75%, with receipts, deadlines, and penalties publicly auditable.
